attempts.text:
{
  "map": true,
  "subject": {"columns": ["protein_id"], "resolver": "pharos_protein_gene", "category": "biolink:Gene"},
  "object": {"columns": ["trait"], "resolver": "pattern:OMIM:Phenotype: .*?(\\d{6}) \\([1-4]\\)", "category": "biolink:Disease", "name_column": "trait"},
  "predicate": "biolink:gene_associated_with_condition",
  "association_category": "biolink:GeneToDiseaseAssociation",
  "knowledge_level": "knowledge_assertion",
  "agent_type": "manual_agent",
  "primary_knowledge_source": "infores:omim",
  "qualifiers": {},
  "edge_properties": ["trait"],
  "keep_if": {"column": "trait", "matches": "Phenotype: ", "reason": "Trait holds only the gene's MIM Number with no phenotype named, so OMIM lists the gene entry without a disease; kept as a recorded gap for the gene, with no disease object."},
  "split_by": null,
  "by_value": {},
  "notes": "Each row is a gene MIM entry from genemap.txt. Only rows whose trait includes 'Phenotype: <name>, <6-digit MIM> (<key>)' name a disease; the object is that phenotype MIM, taken from the text after 'Phenotype:' rather than the leading gene MIM. The mapping key (1-4) is not kept as a qualifier; key 3 means a molecular basis is known, and the key is in the source text if a reader needs it. Some trait cells may be truncated in the export, so the pattern may miss a few. Gene-only rows are recorded as gaps. The predicate is gene_associated_with_condition, which is more specific than the generic gene-disease association."
}
